prompt:
Let $f(x)=x^{2}-4$.

**(a)** Describe how the graph of $y=|f(x)|$ is obtained from $y=f(x)$. **[1]**

**(b)** Describe how the graph of $y=f(|x|)$ is obtained from $y=f(x)$, and explain why it is the same as $y=f(x)$ in this case. **[1]**

**(c)** For $y=\dfrac{1}{f(x)}$, write down the vertical asymptotes and the coordinates of the local maximum. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** Parts below the $x$-axis are reflected in the $x$-axis (here $-2<x<2$) **(A1)**

**(b)** Keep the part for $x\ge0$ and reflect it in the $y$-axis; $f$ is already even, so nothing changes **(A1)**

**(c)** Zeros of $f$ become asymptotes: $x=-2$, $x=2$ **(A1)**; the minimum $(0,-4)$ of $f$ becomes a maximum $\left(0,-\tfrac14\right)$ **(A1)**

Case 1: $2x-3=x+1\Rightarrow x=4$ **(A1)**

Case 2: $2x-3=-(x+1)\Rightarrow x=\tfrac23$ **(A1)**

Check: both give $x+1>0$ (a modulus cannot equal a negative number), so both are valid **(R1)**. $x=4$ or $x=\tfrac23$ **(A1)**

Both sides are non-negative, so squaring preserves the inequality **(R1)**:

$x^{2}-4x+4<4x^{2}+4x+1\Rightarrow3x^{2}+8x-3>0$ **(M1)(A1)**

$(3x-1)(x+3)>0$: $x<-3$ or $x>\tfrac13$ **(A2)**
